_source: PS yearly.pdf (14pp scan, uploaded 2026-09-04) — Pre-school yearly plan, Your Nursery
_method: pymupdf render 200/400dpi -> per-page rotation resolved empirically -> tesseract OCR (multi-threshold union) -> every page confirmed by visual read of the rendered page
_notes: The printed page 5 grid is titled 'Spring 1 - Growth and Change', but the matching narrative page 7 carries a HANDWRITTEN '2' over the half-term number, and page 9 (Animals and Habitats) has its printed '2' struck through and replaced with a handwritten '1'. Both corrections are in Toby's pen. The document therefore resolves to Spring 1 = Animals and Habitats, Spring 2 = Growth and Change; the page 5 heading is an uncorrected typo in the source.
Red/pen ticks throughout are Toby's own annotations and carry no data.
Summer 2 is absent from the PDF entirely — not blank, not unreadable, simply not present.

Summer 2 was absent from PS yearly.pdf and was added on 2026-09-08 (b290) from Summer2_Space_Poster.pdf, which has a real text layer and was parsed, not OCR'd. The parser was proved first against Summer1_Transport_and_Journeys_Poster.pdf, whose five activities it reproduces exactly as b276 already imported them. Summer 2 has NO weekly grid because the poster has none.

weeks.construction: Can we build our houses using different resources? Lego, building blocks, stickle bricks etc.
weeks.art_design: Provide mirrors so children can observe and draw their faces.
weeks.tuff_tray: Sensory bean tray with children's names and body cut outs.

weeks.construction: Constructing ourselves with lego, stickle bricks, popoids etc.
weeks.art_design: Children design their own 'flag' with colours, symbols, drawings that represent them and their favourite things.
weeks.role_play: When I grow up dress up.
weeks.tuff_tray: Face print offs - Loose parts to make random faces, different skin colour, hair colour etc.

weeks.construction: Can the children construct their friends and families faces?
weeks.tuff_tray: Different scenes from across the world. - Small world play.

activities.title: My Plate of Favourite Foods Collage
activities.intent: Encourage children to express their likes and preferences through food choices.
activities.implementation: Provide a paper plate template and a variety of food pictures (fruits, vegetables, meals, treats, etc.) to cut or tear and stick.
activities.impact: Children build confidence in making choices and talking about themselves.
activities.adult_role: Model language, support fine motor skills, and celebrate individuality.

activities.title: Children Create Handprints to Decorate the Room
activities.intent: Help children develop a sense of belonging by contributing to the classroom environment.
activities.implementation: Model the process and provide paints in different colours, paper, and space for handprints.
activities.impact: Children feel pride and ownership in the classroom environment.
activities.adult_role: Model and support, encourage independence, and support turn-taking.

activities.title: Scent Jar Exploration
activities.intent: Encourage children to express likes, dislikes, and preferences.
activities.implementation: Provide small jars/pots with cotton pads scented with a variety of smells (e.g., lavender, mint, lemon, cinnamon).
activities.impact: Children become more confident in expressing choices and feelings.
activities.adult_role: Validate preferences, model exploration, and encourage communication.

activities.title: Emotions Station
activities.intent: Support children's personal, social, and emotional development by helping them recognise and name different feelings.
activities.implementation: Set up a calm area with mirrors, puppets, picture cards of emotions (happy, sad, angry, excited, worried), and sensory toys.
activities.impact: Children become more confident in recognising and labelling their own emotions. They begin to understand that others may feel differently, developing early empathy. They learn strategies for expressing themselves safely and positively.
activities.adult_role: Model emotions, encourage talk, and support empathy.

activities.title: Show and Tell
activities.intent: Build children's confidence in speaking in front of others and sharing something special from home.
activities.implementation: Invite children to bring in a special item (toy, photo, book, etc.).
activities.impact: Children develop confidence in self-expression and listening to others.
activities.adult_role: Prompt with questions, celebrate effort, and model listening.

weeks.construction: Outdoors - Let children use crates, planks, blocks and fabric to make a 'spooky den' or 'haunted house'. Add torches or glow sticks to use inside.
weeks.art_design: Use playdoh to create 'Diwali lamps'. Provide gems, glitter and sequins for the children to decorate them.
weeks.role_play: Diwali Home Corner - Provide tea lights, toy food and flowers. Children can set up their own Diwali celebration. Halloween costume dress up.
weeks.book: Room on the Broom / Binny's Diwali
weeks.tuff_tray: Witches potion making. Diwali coloured rice tray - making rangoli patterns in the rice.

weeks.construction: Palace building - Invite children to build palaces or temples from duplo, blocks, magnets etc.
weeks.art_design: Pumpkin exploration - Provide real pumpkins with spoons and tools for scooping. Painting pumpkins.
weeks.role_play: Bakery shop - Pretend to bake and sell jewish foods using playdoh or toy food.
weeks.tuff_tray: Hanukkah exploration tray. Stars, tea lights, coins, blue rice, scoopers, pictures, words.

weeks.construction: Gift box towers - Use empty boxes or wrapping paper to let the children build and 'wrap' presents.
weeks.art_design: Children design their own 'letters to Santa'. Provide paper, pens, stickers etc.
weeks.role_play: Christmas Post Office - Envelopes, stamps, cards and a posting box. Children role play sorting, and delivering cards and parcels.

activities.title: Create Diwali Lamps
activities.intent: Introduce children to Diwali, the Festival of Lights, and encourage creativity.
activities.implementation: Provide paper, paint and different materials to create small lamps. Once dry, children can decorate with paint and sequins.
activities.impact: Children develop fine motor skills, learn about cultural celebrations, and express creativity.
activities.adult_role: Model how to shape and decorate, explain the Diwali story of light, encourage vocabulary (shiny, smooth, bright), and support fine motor techniques.

activities.title: Firework Painting
activities.intent: Celebrate Bonfire Night and New Year traditions by exploring colour, sound, and movement.
activities.implementation: Use black/dark paper with bright paints. Children use straws, toothbrush flicks, or pom-poms to create firework effects.
activities.impact: Children gain descriptive vocabulary (bang, sparkle, bright), explore expressive art techniques, and improve coordination.
activities.adult_role: Model techniques, introduce expressive words, encourage children to describe what they see, and support turn-taking with resources.

activities.title: Celebration Music and Dance
activities.intent: Encourage children to explore rhythm and movement while learning about different cultural celebrations.
activities.implementation: Play celebration music (e.g., Diwali dance music, Christmas carols, Hanukkah songs). Provide ribbons/scarves to move with the beat.
activities.impact: Children develop rhythm, coordination, and cultural appreciation.
activities.adult_role: Model clapping, dancing, or scarf movements, encourage participation, name instruments, and praise effort and creativity.

activities.title: Christmas Tree Lights and Decorations
activities.intent: Explore how light is used at Christmas and encourage children to take part in festive traditions.
activities.implementation: Provide a small Christmas tree with fairy lights. Children help hang baubles, tinsel, and decorations. Use a switch to turn the lights on together.
activities.impact: Builds a sense of community and belonging, supports fine motor skills, and introduces cultural traditions around light.
activities.adult_role: Model safe handling of decorations, talk about the meaning of Christmas lights, encourage descriptive language (sparkly, twinkly, glowing), and celebrate teamwork when the tree is complete.

activities.title: Lantern Craft and Candle Play
activities.intent: Explore how lanterns and candles are used in different celebrations (Diwali, Hanukkah, Christmas, birthdays).
activities.implementation: Children decorate paper lanterns with tissue paper, card, or foil. Provide battery-operated candles to place inside.
activities.impact: Builds cultural awareness, introduces symbolism of light, and promotes design and making skills.
activities.adult_role: Talk about different traditions, demonstrate safe handling, support cutting and sticking, and celebrate children's designs.

key_books: The Diversity of Life on Earth

weeks.construction: Lego animal houses - Children build a home for an animal of their choice. (den for bear, house for dog, a barn for farm animals).
weeks.art_design: Animal footprint painting - Children dip animals into paint and make footprints.
weeks.role_play: Animal hospital - Children care for animals, pretending to be vets or helpers.
weeks.book: The Diversity of Life on Earth
weeks.tuff_tray: Exploring habitats across the world using sensory materials and animals.

weeks.construction: Build a zoo - Use foam blocks to build different enclosures for the animals.
weeks.art_design: Habitat collage - Children glue natural materials to create habitats. (forest, sea, desert).
weeks.role_play: Zoo keepers - Children take care of zoo animals, clean enclosures and 'feed' animals.

weeks.construction: Jungle bridge/paths - Children create paths, bridges or platforms so that animals can move through their habitat. Can test if the bridge is strong enough for different animals.
weeks.art_design: Animal masks - Children create and decorate animal masks and wear them for a role play activity.
weeks.role_play: Jungle adventure - Children pretend to explore the jungle, climb, hide and move like animals.

activities.title: Small World Animal Habitats
activities.intent: Support children's understanding of where different animals live.
activities.implementation: Provide trays with materials for different habitats (sand for desert, leaves for forest, ice cubes/cotton wool for Arctic, water tray for sea). Add animal figures to match.
activities.impact: Children make connections between animals and environments, developing problem-solving and vocabulary.
activities.adult_role: Model sorting animals into the correct habitats, introduce words (jungle, ocean, desert, cold, hot), and encourage children to explain their choices.

activities.title: Polar Animals Ice Play
activities.intent: Explore Arctic/Antarctic habitats and how animals adapt to cold.
activities.implementation: Freeze small animals in ice blocks; provide warm water droppers/spoons for children to 'rescue' them.
activities.impact: Builds curiosity, fine motor skills, and introduces scientific thinking about melting and cold.
activities.adult_role: Model how to use droppers, introduce words (freeze, melt, slippery, cold), and talk about penguins, polar bears, and seals.

activities.title: Local Habitat Hunt
activities.intent: Help children observe animals in their immediate environment.
activities.implementation: Go outside to look for birds, insects, or worms. Provide magnifying glasses and picture cards.
activities.impact: Builds observation skills, awareness of living things, and respect for nature.
activities.adult_role: Guide safe handling, model using magnifying glasses, extend vocabulary (nest, burrow, shell, wing), and encourage gentle behaviour.

activities.title: Animal Movements Game
activities.intent: Develop gross motor skills and awareness of animal characteristics.
activities.implementation: Call out different animals and encourage children to move like them (jump like a frog, waddle like a penguin, crawl like a bear).
activities.impact: Improves coordination, listening, and imagination.
activities.adult_role: Model movements, join in playfully, and introduce descriptive words (hop, slither, stretch, swing).

activities.title: Animal Patterns Art
activities.intent: Explore how animals' coats and skins help them in their habitats.
activities.implementation: Provide pictures of zebras, giraffes, leopards, snakes, and fish. Children paint or collage animal pattern strips.
activities.impact: Develops observation skills, creativity, and awareness of camouflage.
activities.adult_role: Introduce words (spots, stripes, scales), talk about camouflage in nature, and support painting/cutting skills.

weeks.construction: Children build their own flowers, trees and even gardens using different building resources.
weeks.art_design: Place leaves or bark under paper with crayons for children to discover textures.
weeks.role_play: Flower shop. Provide real or artificial flowers. Add tills, bags, seed packets etc.
weeks.tuff_tray: Plant growth tray - include soil, spades, watering spray, seeds and pots.

weeks.construction: Offer boxes, tubes and pinecones. Children fill and stack them to make little 'homes' for toy bugs.
weeks.art_design: Playdough caterpillars - Provide playdough, beads and sticks so children can make their own caterpillars or other bugs.
weeks.role_play: Bug hunters. Children explore and pretend to care for insects. Use magnifying glasses, nets, bugs.

weeks.construction: Children construct simple 'rain houses' or 'sun tents' with blocks and fabrics.
weeks.art_design: Children draw different types of weather. Provide examples.
weeks.role_play: Rainy day play. Pretend it's raining using umbrellas, wellies, and water sprays.
weeks.tuff_tray: Split the tray into 4 sections for different types of weather. Sand (sun), Blue rice (rain), Cotton wool (rain), Cling film (Wind).

activities.title: Planting Seeds
activities.intent: Help children understand how plants grow and change over time.
activities.implementation: Provide soil, pots, and easy-to-grow seeds (e.g., cress, beans, sunflowers). Children plant seeds and water them regularly.
activities.impact: Children develop responsibility, learn about life cycles, and observe change over time.
activities.adult_role: Model planting, talk about what seeds need to grow, encourage children to describe what they see as plants sprout.

activities.title: How Our Bodies Grow and Change
activities.intent: Support children's awareness of how people grow and change.
activities.implementation: Share baby photos (staff or children if families agree) and compare with how people look now.
activities.impact: Children develop self-awareness, PSED skills, and understanding of time.
activities.adult_role: Facilitate respectful discussions, model vocabulary (baby, child, adult, older), and celebrate children's growing independence.

activities.title: Hatching Eggs
activities.intent: Teach children about animal life cycles and change.
activities.implementation: Have real eggs in an incubator. Track changes each day.
activities.impact: Builds curiosity, patience, and observation skills.
activities.adult_role: Explain the process, encourage gentle handling, guide children to notice changes, and support caring behaviour.

activities.title: Weather Chart and Seasonal Changes
activities.intent: Help children recognise changes in the environment as spring begins.
activities.implementation: Create a daily weather chart; children add symbols for sun, rain, clouds, etc. Discuss how weather affects what we wear and do.
activities.impact: Builds observation skills, supports understanding of seasons and time.
activities.adult_role: Model how to use the chart, extend vocabulary (rainy, cloudy, sunny, warm, cool), and link to children's own experiences.

activities.title: Nature Walk - Signs of Spring
activities.intent: Help children observe seasonal growth in their local environment.
activities.implementation: Take children outside to look for buds, flowers, insects, or changing trees. Collect natural objects like leaves or petals.
activities.impact: Children connect classroom learning to the wider world, developing curiosity and observational skills.
activities.adult_role: Guide observations, introduce descriptive language (bud, blossom, sprout), and encourage children to share what they notice.

weeks.construction: Children design and build a bridge that allows a vehicle to travel from one side to the other.
weeks.role_play: Airport role play area - Chairs as a plane, check in desk, tickets, passports, luggage.

weeks.construction: Use lego, stickle bricks, mobilo to build a vehicle eg train, plane, car, truck.
weeks.art_design: Create a bus or plane ticket for your trip.
weeks.role_play: Train station role play - Children act out buying tickets, waiting, going on a train journey.

weeks.construction: Children construct a garage or parking station for vehicles.
weeks.art_design: Draw and design your own vehicle.
weeks.role_play: Boat adventure - children go on a sea journey, deciding where they are going and what happens on the way.

activities.title: Wheel Printing
activities.intent: Explore transport through creative art.
activities.implementation: Provide toy cars with different wheels to dip in paint and roll across paper.
activities.impact: Children notice patterns, develop fine motor skills, and make creative choices.
activities.adult_role: Model printing, introduce words (tracks, wheels, roll, spin), and encourage descriptive talk.

activities.title: Journey Maps
activities.intent: Support children's understanding of journeys and places.
activities.implementation: Provide large paper and pens to draw simple maps (home to nursery, park, holiday). Add stickers for roads, trees, houses.
activities.impact: Builds early mark making, awareness of place, and sequencing.
activities.adult_role: Model drawing roads/paths, ask questions ('What do we see on the way?'), and encourage storytelling.

activities.title: Traffic Light Game
activities.intent: Develop listening skills, turn-taking, and awareness of road safety.
activities.implementation: Play a stop-and-go game: red = stop, green = go, amber = get ready. Children move around the space as different vehicles.
activities.impact: Builds coordination, listening, and awareness of road safety signs.
activities.adult_role: Model the actions, reinforce safety language (stop, wait, go), and encourage self-regulation.

activities.title: Floating and Sinking Boats
activities.intent: Explore scientific concepts through water play.
activities.implementation: Provide different materials (plastic, foil, wood, sponge) for children to make boats. Test which float or sink.
activities.impact: Encourages prediction, observation, and problem-solving.
activities.adult_role: Model testing, introduce words (float, sink, heavy, light), and ask children to predict outcomes.

activities.title: Transport Songs and Rhymes
activities.intent: Develop rhythm, memory, and language through transport songs.
activities.implementation: Sing rhymes like 'The Wheels on the Bus', 'Row, Row, Row Your Boat', and 'Down at the Station'. Add actions or props.
activities.impact: Children develop rhythm, recall, and confidence in joining group songs.
activities.adult_role: Lead singing, model actions, and praise children for joining in.

activities.title: Rocket Building
activities.intent: Encourage creativity and problem-solving through design.
activities.implementation: Provide junk modelling materials (boxes, tubes, foil) for children to build rockets.
activities.impact: Develops imagination, construction skills, and teamwork.
activities.adult_role: Model joining materials, introduce words (launch, blast, orbit), and encourage children to describe their rockets.

activities.title: Constellation Art
activities.intent: Introduce children to stars and patterns in the night sky.
activities.implementation: Use black paper and chalk/white paint dots to make constellations, linking them with lines.
activities.impact: Builds fine motor control, pattern recognition, and wonder about space.
activities.adult_role: Share simple constellation names, model how to join dots, and encourage storytelling about star shapes.

activities.title: Moon Surface Exploration
activities.intent: Explore textures and sensory play linked to the moon.
activities.implementation: Use flour, sand, or clay to create a 'moon surface' tray. Hide small rocks or 'moon treasures' inside for digging.
activities.impact: Supports sensory exploration, descriptive language, and curiosity.
activities.adult_role: Model using tools, introduce words (crater, dusty, rocky), and encourage descriptive talk.

activities.title: Alien Craft
activities.intent: Support imaginative thinking and creativity.
activities.implementation: Provide craft materials (googly eyes, pipe cleaners, collage shapes) for children to design their own aliens.
activities.impact: Develops fine motor skills, individuality, and storytelling.
activities.adult_role: Model designing, talk about features (antenna, eyes, colours), and encourage children to describe their aliens.

activities.title: Planet Sorting - Size and Colour
activities.intent: Help children notice differences between planets.
activities.implementation: Provide planet cards or balls in different sizes/colours. Children sort them into big/small or group by colour.
activities.impact: Builds early maths (sorting, comparing) and science awareness.
activities.adult_role: Model sorting, use comparative language (bigger/smaller, red/blue), and extend with open questions ('Which planet is the biggest?').
